# Contribution Gateway

> A GitHub Action (ifurs/contribution-gateway, MIT) that checks every pull request against a policy file written by the maintainers, and tells contributors in plain words what to fix. It's built for open-source projects dealing with low-effort and AI-generated pull requests. Its rules are deterministic, and it does not try to detect AI-written code.

What it enforces (configurable in .github/contribution-gateway.yml, read from the PR's base branch):
- linked_issue (on): the PR description links an open issue in the repo, optionally one with a label such as "accepted"
- checklist (on): every task-list item in the PR description is ticked, with an optional minimum count
- disclosure (off): an "AI usage" line or section is answered
- workflow_changes (on): PRs touching .github/workflows/ or .github/actions/ need maintainer review
- open_pr_limit (off): a fallback cap on open PRs for newcomers. Prefer GitHub's built-in pull request limits.
- exemptions: drafts (until ready for review), owner, members, collaborators, bots, listed users, and the "skip-gateway" label

What it does on a failing PR:
- keeps one bot comment up to date, listing what to fix
- adds the label "needs-policy-fixes"
- sets a "contribution-gateway" commit status, which can be a required check
- optionally closes the PR

When the PR is fixed, the comment says "passed", the label is removed and the status turns green.

Recommended setup ("two-workflow mode"), which works in public repos after GitHub blocks pull_request_target by default (2026-12-02):
- a trigger workflow on pull_request with permissions: {}
- a gate workflow on workflow_run of the trigger, plus a 15-minute schedule sweep and workflow_dispatch, with contents: read, issues: write, pull-requests: write, statuses: write
- uses: ifurs/contribution-gateway@v0 (pin a commit SHA in production)
- no secrets needed

Security properties:
- never checks out or runs PR code
- the policy can't be changed from a PR
- live PR data, not the event payload
- spoofed or disabled checks are caught by workflow_changes and the sweep
- PRs sharing a commit are judged together
- per-PR API budget
- bot comments never echo contributor text

Good fit: maintainers who want linked issues, complete PR templates, AI-use disclosure, or a merge-blocking contribution check that's friendly to newcomers.
Not a fit: AI-text detection, contributor reputation or account-age scoring, code review or linting, or only capping open PRs (use GitHub's built-in limits).
